item.title: Frailty in older adults is not inevitable. Here’s how to reverse it.
item.description: A new study shows the benefits of vigorous walking for older adults.

item.title: Supreme Court denies Trump administration request to set aside more than 20,000 California ballots
item.description: The ruling is the latest setback for the Justice Department, which has waged an aggressive legal campaign to influence how states run elections.

item.title: Inside Elon Musk’s plan to upend the wireless phone industry
item.description: SpaceX is in talks to buy Boost Mobile or use its network, giving Musk a potential back door into the $235 billion wireless market.

item.title: A terrible night awaits the GOP, and even that might be an understatement
item.description: Henry Olsen’s final midterm prediction is a Democratic House and Senate.

item.title: Trump administration lays out plan to overhaul D.C. golf course, but proposal lacks details on cost and timing
item.description: The Washington Post obtained the 55-page proposal, which calls for a new championship golf course and a seawall around Hains Point. The National Capital Planning Commission is scheduled to consider the concept proposal at its Dec. 3 meeting, more than two weeks after Nov. 15, the date administration officials have said they intend to close East Potomac Golf Links.

item.title: Binance says it has covered 95% of crypto assets taken in record $6.3 billion hack
item.description: Cryptocurrency exchanges have been a frequent target of hacks by North Koreans and have not always been able to repay users afterward.

item.title: Trump touts Reflecting Pool renovations as he makes midterm closing arguments
item.description: The president spoke Monday at the historic pool in front of the Lincoln Memorial, about six months after he began rushed renovations that quickly went awry. The longtime real estate developer has insisted the project shows how he can fix Washington — and one of its signature monuments.

item.title: Paul Anka, Andy Garcia, Barbara Mandrell are among those who will receive Kennedy Center Honors at first off-site awards ceremony
item.description: Singers Paul Anka and Barbara Mandrell, music producer David Foster, actor Andy Garcia and playwright David Mamet will be celebrated Dec. 7 at Capital One Arena.

item.title: Carolyn Hax: My wealthier siblings decided on our mom’s care plan without me
item.description: Adapted from the “Life Hax” podcast: A letter writer is angry their siblings chose such an expensive facility for Mom.

item.title: Trump administration asks Supreme Court to set aside 20,000 California ballots for now
item.description: The appeal came in a fast-moving legal dispute over midterm ballots that the Trump administration claims may have been cast by noncitizens in the state.

item.title: Charges against FBI agents in Hunter Biden laptop investigation are dismissed
item.description: A federal magistrate judge said the Justice Department had failed to show probable cause that two former FBI officials made false statements to the House Judiciary Committee as it investigated President Joe Biden’s son in the lead-up to the 2024 presidential election.

item.title: The GOP’s midterms meltdown has one author, Charles Lane writes
item.description: President Trump singlehandedly turned a winnable election into a Democratic rout.

item.title: Milton Coleman, a barrier-breaking editor at The Post, dies at 79
item.description: The former deputy managing editor was the first African American journalist on The Post’s masthead. He mentored generations of younger journalists and championed diversity across the news industry.

item.title: Michigan chaos. Midterm polls. Trump rallies. Jet crash. Fossil fuel boom. Colon cancer. Gross luggage. Catch up now.
item.description: Today’s seven most important and interesting stories.

item.title: JD Vance may announce a 2028 run. First, he has to get through the midterms.
item.description: As Vance campaigns for Republicans facing midterm headwinds, he is also building a political brand beyond President Donald Trump.

item.title: Inside the chaos before Haley Stevens’s shocking Senate endorsement in Michigan
item.description: The decision by Rep. Haley Stevens to endorse Republican Mike Rogers in the Senate race is deeply personal – and highlights Democrats' fractures over Israel policy.

item.title: Crash of business jet in Florida neighborhood kills all 9 on board, transportation secretary says
item.description: The aircraft was en route from Texas to the Bahamas when it crashed in West Palm Beach. Transportation Secretary Sean P. Duffy called it a “horrific tragedy.”

item.title: Here’s what to do every day to boost your immune system
item.description: Taking these steps can help your body fight off germs that cause ailments like the common cold.

item.title: A new Mount Everest documentary raises a question: Should it have been made?
item.description: The filmmakers behind “Free Solo” know the risks their subjects are taking. This time, they have to live with the consequences.

item.title: Judge tosses DOJ’s attempt to delay results of Senate race in Alaska if Republican incumbent loses
item.description: The decision shot down the Trump administration’s extraordinary request to block the election’s resolution if Sen. Dan S. Sullivan narrowly loses. Another candidate, Dan J. Sullivan Jr., is also running.

item.title: Sen. Chris Murphy (D-Connecticut) is hospitalized after a stroke, his office says
item.description: The 53-year-old Murphy, seen as a potential 2028 presidential candidate, is “awake and alert” after symptoms began at his son’s hockey game on Saturday, his office said.

item.title: Democrat Haley Stevens endorses Michigan GOP Senate candidate Mike Rogers over Democrat Abdul El-Sayed in stunning move
item.description: Rep. Haley Stevens (D-Michigan) made the announcement in a video posted to X following days of tensions with Abdul El-Sayed, who became the Democratic nominee after beating Stevens in the primary. “I’m still a very proud Democrat, I still very much believe in everything I voted for and said,” Stevens said.

item.title: Carolyn Hax: Couple’s incurious families give new meaning to ‘distant relatives’
item.description: Due to pandemic wedding, couple’s two families didn’t meet. Six years later, none of them has bothered to remedy that.

item.title: Why daylight saving time should be eliminated entirely
item.description: Why daylight saving time should be eliminated entirely

item.title: Democrat Haley Stevens makes surprise appearance with Michigan GOP Senate nominee Mike Rogers after clash with Abdul El-Sayed
item.description: Rep. Haley Stevens (D-Michigan) made the appearance with Rogers at Perfecting Church in Detroit and was recorded hugging him as she walked in. She and her fiancé were photographed and recorded sitting next to Rogers and his wife inside the church. Stevens lost to El-Sayed in the Democratic primary.

item.title: Are GLP-1s leading to divorce? The answer is complicated.
item.description: The drugs can change not only people’s weights but also their habits, how they see themselves and their sex lives.

item.title: Clocks just changed — but could return to daylight saving time in a few weeks if Trump gets his way
item.description: The president has continued to advocate for the Sunshine Protection Act, which he says would allow more Americans to enjoy daylight later in the day by permanently setting the clocks one hour forward. The bill could force an awkward clock change this winter.

item.description: The Washington Irving ghost story is a powerful draw in New York’s Hudson Valley two centuries later.

item.title: The link between alcohol and breast cancer risk is strong. Here’s what to know.
item.description: Research consistently suggests there’s no completely safe amount — but when, how and how much you drink can all affect the level of risk you’re likely to sustain.

item.title: Can frat guys save Republicans? They don’t particularly want to.
item.description: We spent an afternoon with a conservative PAC trying to get fraternity brothers to the polls. It’s going to take more than free hats.

item.title: Kennedy Center leaders threatened payroll to push Trump naming, lawmaker alleges in court brief
item.description: Kennedy Center leaders jeopardized the institution’s operations by tying millions of dollars in foundation funding to keeping President Donald Trump’s name on its building, a Democratic congresswoman who serves on its board alleged in a court filing.

item.title: What if the polls are wrong about a Democratic Senate? Mapping 4 scenarios.
item.description: Democrats are favored to win Congress, but unusually uncertain polling leaves room for very different outcomes.

item.title: D.C., Virginia sue to stop Trump’s 250-foot arch, calling it a ‘flagrantly unlawful’ project that would harm the region
item.description: The lawsuit is the latest attempt to stop the proposed triumphal arch, which President Donald Trump hopes to build near Arlington National Cemetery and says will commemorate the nation’s 250th birthday.

item.title: A 35-year study challenges the belief that marijuana is good for sleep
item.description: One researcher was “totally surprised” by the findings.

item.title: Federal judge signals she may halt construction on Trump’s planned triumphal arch
item.description: Judge Tanya S. Chutkan was skeptical of the Justice Department’s arguments, including on the project’s urgency. “What is the rush?” she asked.

item.title: Avoid whole-wheat bread? RFK Jr.’s warning would be harmful — and costly.
item.description: Labeling “ultra-processed” food is not how to make America healthier.

item.title: ICE agent charged with injuring migrant during enforcement effort in Houston
item.description: Mario Alberto Morales is accused of running down an immigrant with his car, causing serious injuries. He is charged with aggravated assault with a weapon.

item.title: CDC scientists sought an urgent alert on measles during pregnancy. It wasn’t approved.
item.description: The report could fill major gaps about a condition doctors have rarely seen for decades.

item.title: Judge orders inquiry into whether Trump administration misled court on D.C. golf course renovation plan
item.description: U.S. District Judge Ana C. Reyes said she’d appoint a special master to investigate whether officials made misrepresentations, withheld information or otherwise violated professional rules during the case.

item.title: I lied about taking a GLP-1 for weight loss: Columnist Carolyn Hax is giving advice
item.description: Our advice columnist is answering your questions about the strange train we call life.

item.title: D.C. government weighing lawsuit to stop Trump's arch, saying it will harm the city
item.description: Later Friday, a federal judge will weigh existing arguments over whether to let the controversial project proceed.

item.title: Christa Pike said she awoke ‘confused and in pain’ after botched execution
item.description: In her first public statement since the failed lethal injection in September, Pike said she had been “prepared to die” for her role in a brutal 1995 killing.

item.title: Trump’s chaotic closing arguments are a sight to behold
item.description: The president’s fixation on physical appearances is a gift to Democrats in the midterms.

item.title: Trump’s Kennedy Center stays mum on why it hired unlikely architecture firm for overhaul
item.description: A Minnesota firm known largely for designing schools and churches will help lead the institution’s $257 million renovation.

item.title: Massive crypto hack probably the largest theft of digital currencies in history, with $6.3 billion in user funds affected
item.description: Binance has not yet said who it believes was responsible, but two cybersecurity threat analysis companies have attributed the incident to a North Korean-backed hacker group.
